messages:
jordan: FYI — we're seeing sustained fleet saturation in us-west-2 and the support team just received a quota override request from ACME for their launch next Tuesday. Admission control is starting to reject at the edge.
ryan: Confirming metrics from the oncall dashboard — GPU pool utilization ~96% for the past 18m, queue length ~420 requests, p95 gen latency ~800ms. A subset of requests are getting 429s (rate_limited_by_quota).
ryan: Pushed a quick view: `kubectl top pods -n inference | grep gpu` shows pods pegged, and the autoscaler didn't trigger because quota for new nodes is hit in the account.
maya: Ticket created: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/91234 — ACME (acct: acme-enterprise) asking for temporary quota bump to handle a canary of 50 concurrent streams. Sales flagged this as a launch.
jin: @maya thanks — ACME is our Q4 logo push, they want guaranteed capacity for 36 hours around launch. Need a decision fast. What's the cost/risk of a manual override?
ian: Short answer: we can grant a temporary soft-limit override by moving them into a reserved capacity pool or by adjusting per-customer admission thresholds, but we need to protect existing customers. Options: 1) Short-term boost by shifting some dedicated capacity from non-critical tenants (manual, ~2h ops work). 2) Increase global backfill from other regions (cross-region routing) — network egress + latency tradeoffs. 3) Approve override but attach strict SLAs and a chargeback estimate (~$1,600/hr for requested cap).
olivia: From CS: ACME will pay for reserved commit if we can offer predictable perf. They asked for a simple yes/no by EOD. They cannot postpone launch.
maya: On support side we need authorization (ticket notes: biz_approval + finance ok) before flipping quotas. Can we make a temporary policy: allow 50 extra inflight for acme only, and downgrade non-critical realtime jobs to batch?
jordan: We have admission_control config that supports per-tenant limits: `admission_control.max_inflight_per_account`. We can raise ACME's value to 50 for 48h. But must set a global safety net: `total_inflight_cap` stays, so if we hit cluster hard limits other customers will get 429. Is that acceptable?
ryan: Current cluster safety net is 1,000 inflight tokens; raising ACME to 50 won't break that alone, but with current queue length it's risky. If we do a targeted override we should also enable model-fallback routing for ACME to smaller quantized model when latencies spike.
jin: From sales — ACME prefers single-region traffic. Cross-region fallback is risky for their SLO. They want single-region guarantee. If we can't guarantee, they'll take the reserved capacity option. Can ops provision reserved nodes quickly?
ian: Provisioning dedicated nodes in us-west-2 requires quota approvals at cloud provider level; worst-case is 6–12h. Manual reassign within our infra (moving underutilized pools) can be done in ~2h if we get approval from finance for transient overage.
maya: @jordan @ian what's the approval flow? I can escalate to @olivia for customer sign-off and @jin for pricing approval. We need someone from finance to ok temporary charge.
jordan: I'll approve an emergency temporary override if CS and Sales confirm payment and we set auto-revert in 48h. Also require oncall to monitor queue and set alert thresholds: queue > 500 => rollback override.
olivia: ACME confirms payment on record, will sign a short addendum. I filed the signed doc to the ticket.
ryan: I'll deploy the admission change now in canary mode for ACME only, set `max_inflight_per_account=50`, enable fallback to `redwood-small-q4` if p95 > 1s. Watching logs.
SRE-bot: deploy started by ryan at 2024-11-20T15:47:33Z — canary rollout 1/3 nodes.
ryan: Canary looks OK so far, ACME inflight jumped from 6 -> 34, overall queue dropped 18%. No errors yet. Latency for ACME is ~620ms.
jin: Great. Sales: please confirm final billing terms with ACME and mark for reserved-capacity follow-up.
maya: Ticket updated with override notes and rollback plan. I'll keep monitoring and will notify if we hit queue > 500.
jordan: Post-mortem action: we need a runbook to handle these quota override requests and a playbook for quick reserved capacity transfers. Putting it on next sprint. :spiral_calendar: :eyes:
